releases.notes:
## Combat Tracker 1.11.0 — alerts now say which Minecraft version

### Flags carry their version

An alert without a version cannot be read properly. The mod runs on seven Minecraft versions now and they do not all detect the same things — hotbar switching cannot be detected before 1.21.5 — so the same alert means different things depending on where it came from.

Every alert now shows the Minecraft version next to the server, and `/search` lists the versions a player has been seen on.

The version is read from the running game rather than stamped in at build time, so if someone is running a jar built for a different version, that shows.

### README

Every supported version is now listed with its Java requirement, along with a plain explanation of which one is missing hotbar detection and why — rather than leaving someone to notice a check quietly absent.

### Files

| Minecraft | File | Java |
|---|---|---|
| 26.2 | `combat-tracker-26.2.jar` | **25** |
| 1.21.11 | `combat-tracker-1.21.11.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.10 | `combat-tracker-1.21.10.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.9 | `combat-tracker-1.21.9.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.8 | `combat-tracker-1.21.8.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.4 | `combat-tracker-1.21.4.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.1 | `combat-tracker-1.21.1.jar` | 21 |

**Relay operators:** the flag store gains a version column and migrates itself on first run. Redeploy the worker to pick it up.

### Requirements
Fabric Loader >= 0.19.3 · Fabric API · Cloth Config · Mod Menu (optional)

## Combat Tracker 1.10.5 — now on Minecraft 26.2

Seven Minecraft versions. Download the file matching your game; the filename is the version, nothing else to decode.

| Minecraft | File | Java |
|---|---|---|
| **26.2** | `combat-tracker-26.2.jar` | **25** |
| 1.21.11 | `combat-tracker-1.21.11.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.10 | `combat-tracker-1.21.10.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.9 | `combat-tracker-1.21.9.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.8 | `combat-tracker-1.21.8.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.4 | `combat-tracker-1.21.4.jar` | 21 |
| 1.21.1 | `combat-tracker-1.21.1.jar` | 21 |

**26.2 needs Java 25.** Minecraft itself does; the jar states it so your launcher will tell you rather than failing strangely.

### About the 26.2 build

Minecraft 26 rebuilt how the interface draws — the game now collects what to draw and draws it in a second pass. The overlay was rewritten for that, and it now attaches through Minecraft's own HUD system rather than by patching the rendering code, which is a cleaner join than before.

Everything the mod measures is unchanged: jump resets, combo timing, reach, aim placement, and all four input checks work exactly as they do on 1.21.11.

Verified by launching it: the mod loads, the game reaches the menu, and every hook is confirmed attached.

### Still true on 1.21.1 and 1.21.4

Hotbar-switch detection is off on those two. Minecraft has no method there to watch — only a raw number — so it cannot tell your scroll wheel from a macro. Every other check works on all seven.

### Requirements
Fabric Loader >= 0.19.3 · Fabric API · Cloth Config · Mod Menu (optional)

releases.notes:
## Combat Tracker 1.10.4 — detections were being thrown away

If hotbar switches stopped showing up for you, this is the fix. **The detection was working. The alert was being discarded.**

### What was wrong

Alerts are capped at three per session so one bad session cannot flood a channel. But that budget was only ever reset when you started a recording — so if you never record, one budget covered the entire time Minecraft was open. Once it ran out, every later detection was counted and then silently dropped.

In practice: some keybind noise early on used up the three messages, and a hotbar switch an hour later produced nothing at all. From the outside that is indistinguishable from the check not working.

### What changed

A check tripping for the **first time** now always gets a message through, even on a spent budget. There are only four kinds of check, so this cannot flood anything — and staying silent about the first report of a detection is not rate limiting, it is just silence.

The budget also resets when you leave a world, so a "session" now means a world or server visit rather than however long the game has been open.

### Also

The mod version inside the jar was stale — the 1.10.2 and 1.10.3 downloads reported themselves as 1.10.1 to Mod Menu. Corrected.

### Files

| Minecraft | File |
|---|---|
| 1.21.11 | `combat-tracker-1.21.11.jar` |
| 1.21.10 | `combat-tracker-1.21.10.jar` |
| 1.21.9 | `combat-tracker-1.21.9.jar` |
| 1.21.8 | `combat-tracker-1.21.8.jar` |
| 1.21.4 | `combat-tracker-1.21.4.jar` |
| 1.21.1 | `combat-tracker-1.21.1.jar` |

Hotbar detection remains off on 1.21.1 and 1.21.4 — Minecraft has no method there to watch, only a raw number, so it cannot tell your scroll wheel from a macro. Every other check works on all six.

### Requirements
Fabric Loader >= 0.19.3 · Fabric API · Cloth Config · Mod Menu (optional)

releases.notes:
## Combat Tracker 1.10.3 — six Minecraft versions, one release

Download the file matching your game. The filename is the Minecraft version, nothing else to decode.

| Minecraft | File |
|---|---|
| 1.21.11 | `combat-tracker-1.21.11.jar` |
| 1.21.10 | `combat-tracker-1.21.10.jar` |
| 1.21.9 | `combat-tracker-1.21.9.jar` |
| 1.21.8 | `combat-tracker-1.21.8.jar` |
| 1.21.4 | `combat-tracker-1.21.4.jar` |
| 1.21.1 | `combat-tracker-1.21.1.jar` |

Each jar declares the exact version it was built for. That is deliberate rather than a range: the mod hooks into Minecraft by method signature, those signatures moved several times across 1.21.x, and a jar loaded on a version it was not built for fails while hooking in — a crash on startup, not a missing feature.

### One difference on 1.21.1 and 1.21.4

Hotbar-switch detection is off on those two versions, and cannot be made to work there.

On 1.21.5 and later, Minecraft changes your selected slot through a method, which the mod watches to tell an ordinary switch from a scripted one. Before 1.21.5 the slot is just a number the game writes directly, with no method to watch. The only thing left is noticing that the number changed — which cannot tell your scroll wheel from a macro, and would report every scroll and every number key you press. That is noise rather than detection, so it is simply switched off.

Everything else is identical. Item-use, attack and keybind checks all work, as does the check for a slot change sent to the server that your client never made. Jump resets, combo timing, reach and aim are measured exactly the same way on every version.

### Everything else in 1.10.x

The false "keybind pressed by code" alerts are fixed. Releasing a key is no longer counted — letting go of a key cannot make the game do anything, and opening a menu releases every bound key at once, which was producing one alert entry per keybind in your client.

### Requirements
Fabric Loader >= 0.19.3 · Fabric API · Cloth Config · Mod Menu (optional)

## Combat Tracker for Minecraft 1.21.11

Mod version 1.10.1, built against Minecraft **1.21.11**.

Download `combat-tracker-1.21.11.jar`. The file is named for the Minecraft version it targets, so there is no version string to decode — match the number to your game.

This build declares `1.21.11` exactly, not a range. Mixins bind to method signatures and those move within 1.21.x, so a jar loaded on a version it was not built for fails at mixin application, which crashes on startup rather than quietly missing a feature. Use the file that matches your game.

### What's in 1.10.1
Fixes false "keybind pressed by code" alerts. Releasing a key is no longer counted — letting go of a key cannot make the game do anything, and opening a menu releases every key you have bound at once, which was producing one flag per keybind in your client. The check now watches only attack, use, jump, offhand swap and the hotbar slots, leaving sprint, sneak and movement alone since a great deal of ordinary software holds those for you.

### Requirements
Minecraft 1.21.11 · Fabric Loader >= 0.19.3 · Fabric API · Cloth Config · Mod Menu (optional)

releases.notes:
## Combat Tracker v1.9.4

Fewer alerts about the same person.

### Say it once, say it again if it persists, then stop

A player who kept tripping checks produced an alert every 15 seconds, up to twenty in a session. Nineteen of those said nothing the first had not already said — same player, same checks, still going.

The gaps now grow instead: ten seconds after the first flag, then two minutes, then ten, then silence for that session. Three messages rather than twenty.

The short delay on the first one is deliberate. Sending the instant a check trips produces an alert reading "1 hotbar switch", which is the least informative moment there is; ten seconds gathers the opening burst so the first message arrives with real numbers.

Counts in each alert are session totals, not the slice since the last one. A follow-up reporting only the difference would make a player who is still going look like they were tailing off, when in fact only the gaps had grown.

### Nothing else changed

Detection is identical. The report, the JSON and the share link still record every flag with its full timeline — this only changes how often Discord is told, never what is measured or kept.

Share links remain format v4 and every link already shared still opens.

### Requirements
Minecraft 1.21.11 · Fabric Loader >= 0.19.3 · Fabric API 0.141.4+1.21.11 · Cloth Config 21.11.153 · Mod Menu 17.0.0 (optional)

releases.notes:
## Combat Tracker v1.9.2

Alerts are now readable at a glance instead of being a wall of counts.

### A named check, and what it actually means

The previous alert ended in a line like `Tripped: 3 hotbars 1 use`, which tells you how many without telling you what any of it means. Each check that fires now gets its own line saying what was observed:

> **Hotbar switched** ×3
> ╰ *changed slot with no key, scroll or server packet behind it*

Checks that did not fire are left out entirely rather than printed as zeroes.

### Who, not just what

Alerts are Discord embeds now. They carry the player's head, so one is identifiable without reading a UUID, and a **Fighting** field naming the opponent.

The opponent comes from whoever was last swung at or hit, and it expires after fifteen seconds. A name from four minutes ago is not who you were fighting when a check tripped, and printing it as though it were would put an uninvolved player's name in someone else's alert. Past that window it says there is no recent opponent, which is the honest answer.

Timestamps are sent as an instant rather than a fixed timezone, so Discord renders them in each reader's own local time.

### Unchanged

The four checks — hotbar switches, item uses, attacks, and keybinds pressed by code rather than by a key — work exactly as they did in v1.9.1, including the fix there for a slot change that is undone inside a single tick.

What is sent is also unchanged: your Minecraft name and UUID, the server address, the time, how many checks tripped, and who you were fighting. Nothing else. There is no setting to turn it off, because the only person who would turn it off is the one it would be reporting on. If you would rather not be reported on, don't install it.

An unattributed action is still not by itself proof of cheating. Controller support and accessibility mods drive the game by setting keybinds, and produce a steady keybind count with nothing wrong at all. That caveat now lives in the report and the settings screen, where there is room to explain it, rather than on the end of every alert.

Share links are unchanged at format v4. Every link you have already shared still opens.

### Requirements
Minecraft 1.21.11 · Fabric Loader >= 0.19.3 · Fabric API 0.141.4+1.21.11 · Cloth Config 21.11.153 · Mod Menu 17.0.0 (optional)

releases.notes:
## Combat Tracker v1.9.1

A fix to the hotbar check from v1.9.0, and the first release whose downloads actually report.

### The hotbar check looked once per tick, and that wasn't enough

The selected slot was compared against its expected value at the end of each tick. That catches a switch that stays put, but not one that is undone before the tick ends — write the slot, swing, write it back, and the tick finishes exactly where it started, so the comparison saw no change at all. That is the shape of an auto-disable: switch to an axe, hit, switch back.

The slot is now also read at the moment an action is taken — on every attack and item use — where the discrepancy is still there to see. A swap that is undone within a tick is caught at the swing rather than being invisible.

The bookkeeping behind this moved into its own class with no game code in it, and the cases that have gone wrong before are now tests that run without launching Minecraft: a legitimate scroll in the same tick must not excuse a cheat's switch, and a respawn must not read as a hotbar change. Both were real bugs during development; neither can come back silently now.

### Reporting works in this download

v1.9.0 shipped with no reporting endpoint set, so that build sent nothing anywhere. This one reports through a relay, which keeps the destination out of the jar.

As always, and stated in the settings screen and the README: when a check trips, this sends your Minecraft name and UUID, the server address, the UTC time, and how many checks tripped. Nothing else. There is no setting to turn it off, because the only person who would turn it off is the one it would be reporting on. If you would rather not be reported on, don't install it.

### Unchanged from v1.9.0

The four checks — hotbar switches, item uses, attacks, and keybinds pressed by code rather than by a key — work the same way, and mean the same thing. An unattributed action is not by itself proof of cheating: controller support and accessibility mods drive the game by setting keybinds, and produce a steady keybind count with nothing wrong at all. Read the other three rows first.

Share links are unchanged at format v4. Every link you have already shared still opens.

### Requirements
Minecraft 1.21.11 · Fabric Loader >= 0.19.3 · Fabric API 0.141.4+1.21.11 · Cloth Config 21.11.153 · Mod Menu 17.0.0 (optional)

releases.notes:
## Combat Tracker v1.8.1

Nothing about how the mod measures a fight has changed. This is a fix to the tool that rebuilds links from saved reports, and a rewrite of the claims the documentation was making.

### Reports are checked before they become links

`linkifyReports` read the canonical data out of a saved report and rebuilt a share link from it without ever checking the SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA256 written into that same file a few lines above. Editing the figures in a text editor and running the tool produced a clean-looking link, while the untouched hash still described the data the report used to hold. That made it the easiest way to launder edited numbers.

It now recomputes both, and writes a link only for a report that still matches its own hashes. Anything it cannot check is refused rather than quietly downgraded — a missing integrity block, an unreadable one, or two canonical blocks where there should be one — and a run with refusals exits non-zero. A link carries no verdict of any kind, so a link written for a report that failed to verify would be indistinguishable from any other one once it left the machine that made it.

The command is unchanged:

```
./gradlew linkifyReports -PlinkifyDir="path/to/reports"
```

**Be clear about the size of this.** It catches a corrupted file, and it catches someone editing a report in a text editor. It does not catch someone who edits the numbers *and* recomputes the two values, because the HMAC key is a string literal in this repository. There is nothing secret in it.

Two smaller fixes in the same area. The unescape step was not the inverse of the escaping the report writer uses — `&` is escaped first, so `&` has to be undone last, and undoing it first corrupted any data containing the literal text `<`. Left as it was, the new check would have failed reports nobody had touched. Whitespace around the canonical block is now told apart from a real mismatch too, so reformatting a report is not reported as forgery. `tools/LinkifyReports.java` is gone: a stale duplicate in no source set that carried the same bypass, crashed on any successful run, and could only ever have drifted from the copy that actually runs.

### The documentation was overclaiming

The caveats said that forging a report required recompiling the mod. That was wrong, and wrong in the direction that made people trust these reports more than they should.

- **Share links carry no signature at all.** The payload is deflate + base64url of the struct the README documents, and the viewer's only check is that the version byte is one it knows. A link can be written from scratch in about a hundred lines of Python, in any name, and the page will fetch that player's real skin to go with it. No mod and no recompile.
- **The saved files are a checksum, not a seal.** They catch corruption and casual editing. See above for where that stops.
- **The viewer does not re-derive the headline numbers** from the plotted points; it prints what the link carries. On a link you did not make yourself, check that the cards and the graph agree.
- **The name and skin at the top of a link are just text in the payload**, so a link can be made to look like someone else's.
- **"Nothing gets uploaded" now names its one exception**: the page fetches player heads from `mc-heads.net`, so that service sees the names on a report. The fight data itself genuinely never leaves your browser.

The framing throughout is now what the tool actually is. It shows the shape of a fight — scattered aim against a knot on centre, timing that wanders against timing that does not — and that reads off a chart in ten seconds where it takes twenty minutes of clips. To someone who already has reason to take you seriously it is worth a lot. To someone who doesn't, it is worth nothing, and you should expect them to say so. It is a record, not proof.

### Requirements

...
